description: Surface Optimization of the (100) Surface of Orthorhombic Mo2C (beta-Mo2C, Pbcn) and Surface Energy Calculation
user_prompt: Optimize the (100) surface of orthorhombic molybdenum carbide beta-Mo2C (Pbcn) and calculate the surface energy. Report the final surface energy in J/m^2.

references: Politi, Vines, Rodriguez & Illas, Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 15, 12617 (2013)
method.modeling: orthorhombic beta-Mo2C (Pbcn); nonpolar (100) surface; stoichiometric slab, two outermost layers relaxed.
method.rationale: Value 3.03 J/m^2 is the relaxed PBE surface energy of the nonpolar orthorhombic beta-Mo2C(100) face from Politi et al. 2013 (VASP, PAW-PBE), which reports a cleavage energy Ecl = 6.06 J/m^2; for nonpolar surfaces gamma = Ecl/2 = 3.03 J/m^2. beta-Mo2C (orthorhombic) is the experimentally dominant Mo2C polymorph; its most stable nonpolar facet is the lower-energy (011) (gamma 1.82). Metallic carbide requires Methfessel-Paxton smearing. Tolerance +/-0.3 J/m^2 (absolute, ~10%) covers PBE inter-setup scatter and xc-functional sensitivity.
